clue.text: Musical composed only of Earth sign symbols

parts.words: Musical composed only of Earth sign symbols
parts.note: surface reading: a show written about the zodiac, built from the glyphs for Taurus, Virgo and Capricorn

parts.words: composed only of Earth sign symbols
parts.note: setter's reading: the title is spelt using nothing but the letters found in the two words EARTH SIGN

explanation.surface: An astrological musical whose score is written in the symbols of the earth signs.
explanation.walkthrough: The symbols are not zodiac glyphs but letters: every letter of the title is one of E, A, R, T, H, S, I, G, N, repeated as often as needed.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1952 Gene Kelly film became a celebrated stage musical, so the title is an example of a musical.

clue.text: Promise to hide skin, pulling up pajamas

indicators.note: to hide something is to keep it covered inside, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: to promise is to swear

indicators.note: in a down entry, pulling something up reads it from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to skin fruit is to peel it

explanation.surface: A vow to conceal a bare body while hauling on night clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'pulling up' reverses the word, since it is read from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleepwear is the collective word for clothes worn in bed, pajamas included.

clue.text: Bill gets left with Nick

indicators.note: the first word gets, or receives, the next one into itself

parts.note: a bill is a banknote
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Bill leaves together with Nick: two men's names going off together.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill and Nick look like two men; Bill is a banknote and Nick is the definition, the actor Nick Nolte.
explanation.definitionFit: Nick Nolte is the American film actor, so his first name defines his surname.

clue.text: I am in favor of victory in Europe? Correct

parts.note: contracted to I'm
pro means for, in favour of
VE Day marked Victory in Europe in 1945

explanation.surface: Someone declaring support for a European triumph and asking if that's right.
explanation.definitionFit: To correct something is to fix its faults, which is to make it better.

clue.text: Questionnaire nearly reveals girl's name

indicators.note: to reveal is to uncover something already there, so the letters lie inside the words before

parts.note: the tail of the first word joined to the start of the second

explanation.surface: A survey form almost gives away a young woman's name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' looks like it should shorten Questionnaire, but it is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Irene is a female first name, from the Greek word for peace.

clue.text: Drummer Burton: negative review is carried by Time

indicators.note: being carried by something means being held within it, so the rest sits inside the last word

parts.note: Tim Burton, the film director
to pan a show is to slate it
taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A drummer called Burton gets a bad write-up in Time magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drummer Burton' reads as one person, but Drummer is the definition and Burton is the film director.
explanation.definitionFit: A timpanist plays the timpani, the kettledrums of an orchestra, so is a drummer.

clue.text: Like New Jersey, dysfunctional Senate welcomes Republican

indicators.note: welcoming someone means taking them inside, so one letter goes in among the others
something dysfunctional is not working in its proper order, so its letters get jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
R is the abbreviation for a Republican

explanation.surface: A jab at New Jersey's broken state legislature letting in a Republican.
explanation.walkthrough: The Republican's R joins the letters of SENATE before they are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: New Jersey lies on the US Atlantic seaboard, so it is an eastern state.

clue.text: Single-purpose computer program concerning energy for a plant

parts.note: an applet is a small application that does one job
re means concerning, as in a letter heading
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A software description: a single-use program about power use in a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' sounds industrial alongside energy, but it is the living kind.
explanation.definitionFit: An apple tree is a fruit-bearing tree, and a tree is a plant.

clue.text: Smart like Turner?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: neat and stylish in dress
second meaning, playful: resembling Nat Turner, leader of the 1831 slave revolt in Virginia

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone dressed sharply looks like a famous Turner.
explanation.walkthrough: Turner suggests the painter or Tina, but the clue wants Nat Turner; adding -TY to his first name gives 'like Nat'.
explanation.definitionFit: Natty is an informal adjective for neatly and fashionably dressed, and jokingly also 'Nat-like'.

clue.text: Oval Office's ending with backward tumble? Excellent

indicators.note: going backward means the synonym is written from its last letter to its first
the ending of a word is its final letter, so only the last letter of the possessive word is kept

parts.note: the last letter of Office
a tumble is a spill, a fall
E is a school grade meaning excellent in some American grading schemes

explanation.surface: A question about what follows when the President's office ends with someone taking a fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oval Office' reads as one place, but Oval is the definition and Office only supplies a letter. The reversed SPILL sits between two Es to give ELLIPSE.
explanation.definitionFit: An ellipse is the geometric name for a regular oval shape, a flattened circle.

clue.text: Most hip dancing?!

indicators.note: letters that are dancing are jumping about, so the two words before it get rearranged

parts.note: taken as written: seven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A claim that a certain way of dancing is the trendiest of all.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does both jobs: the jumbled words build the answer, and the whole phrase describes the place where the coolest, wildest dancing at a rock gig happens.
explanation.definitionFit: A mosh pit is the area in front of a stage where fans slam-dance, a hip kind of dancing.

clue.text: "Ladies Only" in random heap for special events

indicators.note: one item placed in another sits inside it, splitting the outer letters
something random has no set order, so the next word's letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged as PHEA
a ladies-only space admits no men

explanation.surface: A 'Ladies Only' sign tossed into a jumble of junk.
explanation.walkthrough: A sign reading 'Ladies Only' amounts to saying no men are allowed.
explanation.definitionFit: Phenomena are remarkable occurrences or happenings, which the clue calls special events.

clue.text: Poem that laments Israel-Egypt connection

indicators.note: the connection between two names is the join where they meet, and the letters spanning that join are read

parts.note: the end of Israel run on into the start of Egypt

explanation.surface: A mournful verse about relations between Israel and Egypt.
explanation.definitionFit: An elegy is a poem of mourning, typically for someone who has died.

clue.text: Revision of 19A, for example:

definitions.note: the definition is the phrase that introduces a list, standing for the list itself

indicators.note: a revision reworks and reorders material, so the referenced entry's letters are rearranged

parts.note: the answer to the climber clue at 19 across

explanation.surface: An editorial note that a later answer has been rewritten, offered as an example.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon is part of the definition: 'for example:' is what you write just before an enumeration, a list of items.
explanation.definitionFit: An enumeration is a list of items one by one, which is what follows the words 'for example' and a colon.

clue.text: Nasty clue: "Women getting frowned upon"

indicators.note: something nasty has been messed about with, so the letters of the words that follow are mangled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A self-referential complaint about a mean crossword clue whose subject is disapproval of women.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make it look like a clue being quoted; the words inside it are the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unwelcome is not wanted, and so frowned upon by those it reaches.

clue.text: Superior description of disease involving blood types (five)

indicators.note: involving means including, so the description's letters wrap around what follows

parts.note: an acute illness is sudden and severe
AB and O are two blood groups
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A medical note about an illness affecting blood groups, five of them.
explanation.walkthrough: ACUTE is split after its T to take in AB, O and V.
explanation.definitionFit: Being a cut above is an idiom for being better than others, so superior.

clue.text: Create a new image of doubly rare…

parts.note: rare steak is red in the middle; the clue asks for two words that each mean rare
underdone meat is also called raw, the second meaning of rare

explanation.surface: Making a fresh picture of something that is twice as uncommon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rare' here is the cooking sense, not 'uncommon'; doubly means two synonyms for it are joined.
explanation.definitionFit: To redraw something is to sketch it again, producing a fresh picture of it.

clue.text: Move quickly with silver and bread for musketeer

parts.note: to dart is to dash
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
naan, also spelt nan, is an Indian flatbread

explanation.surface: Dashing off with the silverware and a loaf.
explanation.definitionFit: D'Artagnan is the young Gascon hero who joins the Three Musketeers in Dumas's novel.

clue.text: See 16
…climber, seeing 13 differently

indicators.note: seeing something differently means arranging it another way, so the referenced entry is reordered

parts.note: the answer to 13 across

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: a climber with a new perspective on things.
explanation.walkthrough: This clue and 13 across are anagrams of each other, so solving either one gives the letters of the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A mountaineer is a person who climbs mountains for sport.

clue.text: Bond's boss is thrown in the wrong role

parts.note: M is James Bond's chief at MI6
taken as written
something thrown is cast

explanation.surface: Complaining that the actor playing 007's chief has been badly chosen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown' tempts as an anagram signal, but here it is a synonym: cast.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor who is miscast has been given a part that does not suit them.

clue.text: Some schools restricting gold teeth

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem in, so the outer word holds the other within it

parts.note: Ivy League colleges are called the Ivies
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Elite schools limiting how much gold dental work students may have.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ivy League is the group of old, elite universities in the north-eastern US, such as Harvard and Yale.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivories is informal slang for teeth, from their white colour.

clue.text: Listening to spirits, we step on them

indicators.note: listening means the word is heard rather than read, so its sound is what counts

parts.note: spirits are souls, which sounds the same as the word needed

explanation.surface: A spooky picture of trampling on ghosts we can hear.
explanation.definitionFit: The soles of our feet, or shoes, are the part we tread on when walking.

clue.text: It's "in"—hipsters' language!

indicators.note: saying it is in tells the solver the word sits inside the letters that follow

parts.note: the last letter of the first word run on into the start of the second

explanation.surface: Someone excitedly declaring a hipster way of speaking fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: 'in', meaning trendy, is itself a piece of hip talk, and the answer is literally in the words that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang is the informal vocabulary of a social group, such as the trendy talk of hipsters.

clue.text: Princess and prosecutor taking in capital

indicators.note: taking something in means swallowing it, so a further word goes inside the letters before it

parts.note: taken as written
the Italian capital city
a district attorney, the American public prosecutor

explanation.surface: A princess and a lawyer drawn into a big city.
explanation.walkthrough: AND plus DA together take in ROME: AND, ROME, DA.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Andromeda was an Ethiopian princess rescued from a sea monster by Perseus.

clue.text: Thwart serial killer on TV, losing adult rating

indicators.note: losing something means it is gone, so one letter is taken out of the name

parts.note: Dexter Morgan, title character of the TV series Dexter
X was the film rating for adults only

explanation.surface: Stopping a TV murderer, whose show loses its grown-ups-only rating.
explanation.definitionFit: To deter someone is to put them off acting, which can thwart a plan.

clue.text: Disgusting lice devouring love bug

indicators.note: devouring something takes it inside, so one letter is swallowed by the others
something disgusting is foul and messed up, so the next word's letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
love is zero in tennis scoring, the letter O

explanation.surface: Revolting parasites gobbling up an insect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bug' looks like an insect, matching the lice, but here it means a germ.
explanation.definitionFit: E. coli is a bacterium that can cause food poisoning, and bug is informal for a germ.

clue.text: Fruit and eggs returned by rotter along with bagel

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word is written in the opposite direction

parts.note: ova is Latin for eggs
a cad is a rotter, a dishonourable man
a bagel is ring-shaped, like the letter O

explanation.surface: A breakfast order: fruit and eggs sent back by a scoundrel, with a bagel.
explanation.walkthrough: The bagel's ring shape stands for the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: An avocado is the pear-shaped fruit of a tropical tree, often eaten on toast or bagels.

clue.text: Eric, dropping Ecstasy, wears lacerated hat

indicators.note: whatever is worn surrounds the wearer, so the name sits inside the other word

parts.note: something lacerated is torn

indicators.note: dropping something means letting it fall away, so a letter leaves the name

parts.note: taken as written, before losing a letter
E is the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Eric gives up drugs and puts on a ripped hat.
explanation.walkthrough: Ecstasy is the drug, and as is usual in crosswords it stands for the letter E.
explanation.definitionFit: A tricorn is a three-cornered hat with the brim turned up, worn in the 18th century.

clue.text: Economic catastrophe in the Grand Canyon?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the worldwide slump of the 1930s
second meaning, read literally: a huge hollow in the land; the question mark flags the playful reading

explanation.surface: A financial collapse playing out in Arizona's famous gorge.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a literal reading: a canyon is a very big dip in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1930s slump is the classic economic disaster, and a vast canyon is literally a huge sunken hollow in the landscape.
